business-api-context · map

Business API map

What each endpoint group means to the business: who calls it, what it changes, which auth level it needs.

Overview

This API is how a QA team turns a backlog into an executable, auditable test operation. Teams bring structure in (from Jira or by hand), author Acceptance Test Cases, assemble them into suites and release-scoped plans, execute runs, file native bugs, and publish verdicts and coverage — all through one versioned surface (/api/v1) that the product UI itself consumes. The business does not "call an API"; it performs QA operations, and every one of them lands here.

Three kinds of callers share the same surface: browsers on a Supabase session cookie (the product), scripts and CI/CD on personal access tokens (bk_pat_*), and inbound machine callers — Stripe webhooks and Vercel Cron — which authenticate with a signature or a shared secret instead of a user. One identity resolver (resolveIdentity()) folds cookie and token callers into the same Principal, so authorization behaves identically no matter who knocks. A fourth, narrower posture exists for owner-level operations: the gateway can structurally reject Bearer tokens (auth: 'cookie-only') so a PAT can never mint another PAT, delete a workspace, or pull a tenant export.

The business-critical edges are few and sharp: onboarding is gated on an email leaving Supabase Auth/Resend; revenue is gated on a signed Stripe webhook being accepted and de-duplicated; run verdicts feed the coverage numbers the business reports; and workspace export/deletion can move or destroy an entire tenant's data. Everything else is authoring CRUD sitting behind Row Level Security and per-route capability checks.

Permission & auth model

AuthN has two user rails plus two machine rails; AuthZ is Postgres RLS plus four capability scopes enforced at the gateway. Every non-public route states its posture at compile time — there is no default.

Tiers

Tier Who it applies to How to acquire Where enforced (code path)
Public Anonymous visitors, Stripe, Vercel Cron None — auth: 'public' routes (signup, signin, magic-link, confirm, resend, check-email, health, API index, OpenAPI doc); Stripe adds a signature; Cron adds CRON_SECRET Gateway skips identity entirely (lib/api/handler.ts); signature check in app/api/v1/billing/webhook/route.ts (constructEventAsync over raw body); isValidCronSecret() in lib/notifications/send-digest-run.ts, called from app/api/v1/admin/send-digest/route.ts (GET + POST, both gated)
Session cookie Browser users of the product Password (POST /api/v1/auth/signin), magic link (POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link → GET /auth/callback), signup (POST /api/v1/auth/signup), OAuth GitHub/Google (/auth/oauth/[provider] → /auth/callback) middleware.ts (edge: session refresh, page redirects on /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity) → resolveIdentity() in lib/api/principal.ts (SSR Supabase client; cookie principal holds all capabilities)
Bearer PAT Scripts, CI jobs, AI agents POST /api/v1/tokens (cookie-only); plaintext bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret> shown once; SHA-256 hash stored in access_token_secrets, prefix indexed on access_tokens lib/api/middleware/bearer.ts (prefix lookup + constant-time hash compare + revoke/expiry checks) → resolveIdentity() mints a short-lived user JWT (lib/api/user-jwt.ts, SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET) so RLS sees auth.uid() identically to cookies
Cron secret Vercel Cron scheduler (and manual same-day retry) CRON_SECRET env var sent as Authorization: Bearer Route is auth: 'public' (BK-214 / ADR-0017 system principal); the real gate is isValidCronSecret() inside the handler — no user principal exists
Webhook signature Stripe (inbound) stripe-signature header over the raw body constructEventAsync() in app/api/v1/billing/webhook/route.ts — the only auth on that route; auth: 'public'

Capabilities and postures

The capability vocabulary is four scopes (lib/api/capabilities.ts, CHECK-constrained in migration 0008_access_tokens.sql): atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin. A cookie session implicitly holds all four; a PAT holds an explicit subset. Workspace roles (viewer / member / admin / owner on workspace_members) are enforced by Postgres RLS — handlers do not re-implement role checks in TypeScript; requireCapability() / assertWorkspaceContext() only constrain PAT callers in practice.

The gateway (withApiHandler) admits exactly four postures, and a route cannot compile without choosing one: public, cookie-only (Bearer structurally rejected — token issuance and revocation, active-workspace switch, membership leave, workspace delete/restore, data-export and its download), authenticated (no capability — bootstrap workspace, me, invites accept, notifications, token list), and required with a non-empty requires list (the bulk of the surface). A PAT scoped to workspace A cannot act on workspace B (assertWorkspaceContext); a token with no workspace binding cannot perform workspace-admin operations at all — there is no global admin (ADR-0005).

No refresh token exists for PATs: revoke = delete the row (DELETE /api/v1/tokens/[id], cookie-only). Cron and webhook tiers have no user principal — each gates a single route family.

Journey: New QA team signs up and gets a workspace

Purpose: a QA engineer provisions an account and a first workspace in seconds — the front door to every other flow.

  1. User authenticates by password, magic link/OTP, or OAuth; Supabase Auth sets the refresh cookie that every later call resolves.
  2. POST /api/v1/workspaces bootstraps the first workspace and membership rows, so RLS has something to authorize against. This is the one capability-free write in the API (auth: 'authenticated') — a brand-new principal must be able to land somewhere before any scope exists.
  3. From here the user is a viewer until invited or promoted — membership is the unit of access.

Endpoints involved:

  • POST /api/v1/auth/signin, POST /api/v1/auth/signup, POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link, POST /api/v1/auth/confirm, POST /api/v1/auth/resend, POST /api/v1/auth/check-email — all public
  • GET /auth/callback, GET /auth/oauth/[provider] — OAuth/magic-link completion (app-level, not /api/v1)
  • POST /api/v1/workspaces — authenticated (bootstrap)
  • GET /api/v1/workspaces — atc:read (list with the caller's role per workspace)

Entities touched: workspaces, workspace_members · Feature IDs: FEAT-AUTH-001…005, FEAT-WS-001

Why it matters: if email delivery or bootstrap fails, nobody gets in — the entire system is gated behind workspace membership, and a silent Resend drop looks like "the product is down".

Journey: QA lead invites a teammate with a role

Purpose: an admin expands the team with the right permission level — the main way authority propagates.

  1. Admin (workspace:admin capability + RLS admin/owner role) issues an invite via POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites; invite email is not wired — the API returns an accept_url for copy-link sharing (unre-verified this pass, see discovery-gaps).
  2. Teammate exchanges the token at POST /api/v1/invites/accept (auth: 'authenticated' — any signed-in user may accept; the token itself is the proof). Role lands via upsert on workspace_members.
  3. Invites are manageable per-id (GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/[inviteId], workspace:admin), enabling revoke and correction.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites, GET /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites, GET /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/[inviteId], PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/[inviteId], DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/[inviteId], POST /api/v1/invites/accept · Entities: workspace_invites, workspace_members · Features: FEAT-WS-002

Why it matters: permission changes are a security-class flow; integrity bugs BK-60/61/62 (member-uniqueness, duplicate invites, role overwrite) were recorded against this chain in the legacy map and remain the weakest application-level checks — retest candidates.

Journey: Workspace upgrades its plan through Stripe Checkout

Purpose: the revenue path — a workspace buys the cloud plan, seats included, and the entitlement flips when Stripe confirms.

  1. Admin (workspace:admin) calls POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/billing/checkout. Idempotency-Key is REQUIRED (ADR-0002); an open checkout attempt is inserted first (partial unique: one open session per workspace), then the Stripe session is created and its id backfilled.
  2. Payment happens entirely on Stripe's hosted page — card data never touches this API.
  3. Stripe delivers POST /api/v1/billing/webhook. The only authentication is the signature over the raw body (constructEventAsync). Handled types: checkout.session.completed, .async_payment_succeeded (plan applies only when Stripe's payment_status is paid), .async_payment_failed, .expired (both release the open-session lock); anything else is acked 200 and ignored.
  4. Application is delegated to the RPC applyBillingCheckoutWebhookEvent with an event-id fence (duplicate delivery → no-op). unknown_session answers 5xx so Stripe redelivers rather than a not-yet-committed row being swallowed as a duplicate.
  5. Cancel path (POST .../billing/checkout/cancel, workspace:admin) closes the open attempt so a later checkout is not blocked.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/billing/checkout, POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/billing/checkout/cancel, GET /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/billing, POST /api/v1/billing/webhook · Entities: billing_checkout_sessions, stripe_webhook_events · Features: FEAT-BILL-001…003

Why it matters: revenue path with async settlement — webhook idempotency and seat-upgrade collisions (SQLSTATE 45700 class) are the high-risk points; a lost event means a paid customer without entitlement.

Journey: Engineer authors tests, executes a run, gets a verdict

Purpose: the core product loop — author ATCs, assemble suites and plans, run them, mark steps, finish with a verdict that rolls into coverage, and file native bugs from failures.

  1. Authoring creates ATCs through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (POST /api/v1/atcs, atc:write) — steps and assertions land in one transaction; optimistic version returns 409 on stale writes (PATCH /api/v1/atcs/[id]). ATC list/search live under /api/v1/atcs/search; duplicate and usage helpers hang off /api/v1/atcs/[id]/….
  2. A Test chains ATCs (POST /api/v1/tests, atc:write, Idempotency-Key REQUIRED); suites assemble into plans (POST /api/v1/test-plans/[id]/tests, also idempotency-required).
  3. A run snapshots its ATCs and steps (run_atcs, run_steps) via POST /api/v1/runs (run:execute, Idempotency-Key REQUIRED plus a 24h start_token fence on (test_id, start_token)) so later library edits never rewrite run history.
  4. Step marks are legal only from pending (POST /api/v1/runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark, run:execute); finish forces leftovers to skipped and computes the verdict (POST /api/v1/runs/[id]/finish); abort stops mid-flight (POST /api/v1/runs/[id]/abort). Abandoned runs are reaped by a pg_cron sweep so the state machine always terminates.
  5. Failures feed native bug filing (POST /api/v1/bugs, atc:write) anchored to module + optional run/step/ATC provenance; triage moves status (POST /api/v1/bugs/[id]/status) and assignment (POST /api/v1/bugs/[id]/assign).

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/atcs, PATCH /api/v1/atcs/[id], GET /api/v1/atcs/search, POST /api/v1/atcs/[id]/duplicate, GET /api/v1/atcs/[id]/usage, POST /api/v1/tests, POST /api/v1/test-plans/[id]/tests, POST /api/v1/runs, POST /api/v1/runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark, POST /api/v1/runs/[id]/finish, POST /api/v1/runs/[id]/abort, POST /api/v1/bugs, POST /api/v1/bugs/[id]/status, POST /api/v1/bugs/[id]/assign · Entities: atcs, atc_steps, atc_assertions, tests, test_plans, test_plan_tests, runs, run_atcs, run_steps, bugs · Features: FEAT-ATC-001…006, FEAT-TEST-001, FEAT-TPLAN-001/002, FEAT-RUN-001…004, FEAT-COV-001, native bug features

Why it matters: this is the value proposition; a broken run chain or a stuck running row distorts every coverage number the business reports. Read/aggregate surfaces (/api/v1/projects/[id]/coverage, /traceability, /runs/report, /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/coverage, /active-runs, /api/v1/activity, /api/v1/search) all hang off the same execution data.

Journey: Team imports its Jira backlog

Purpose: migration onboarding — existing epics/issues become Bunkai user stories linked to modules, without manual re-entry.

  1. POST /api/v1/imports (atc:write) only enqueues: identity check, single-active-job fence (BK-142 class), insert — response returns immediately with the job id.
  2. A deferred after() worker pulls issues over Jira's REST API (raw fetch in lib/jira, no SDK) and upserts stories keyed by external_id.
  3. Progress is polled at GET /api/v1/imports/[id] (atc:read); per-issue errors accumulate while the job still completes (partial import is accepted by design). There is no collection list route anymore — only the single-job poll (drift vs legacy, see discovery-gaps).

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/imports, GET /api/v1/imports/[id] · Entities: import_jobs, user_stories, modules · Features: FEAT-JIRA-001 (Beta)

Why it matters: import is the migration onboarding path; missing Jira credentials fail the whole job (BK-142 on staging) and the worker dies silently with the function if Vercel kills it mid-flight.

Journey: Admin exports or deletes a workspace

Purpose: data-egress and offboarding — pull a full tenant archive, or remove the tenant entirely with a recovery window. Owner-level, cookie-session-only end to end (BK-508): a PAT is rejected regardless of scope.

  1. POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/data-export (auth: 'cookie-only', owner-authorized via assertExportAuthorized) inserts a job row and returns 202; at most one active export per workspace (409 export_in_progress).
  2. A Vercel after() worker (lib/workspace-export/export-runner.ts) builds the archive and uploads it to Supabase Storage; status advances on workspace_exports (GET .../data-export polls the latest job; "expired" is derived client-side from expires_at, never a stored status).
  3. GET .../data-export/download verifies and streams while the expiry holds.
  4. DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/[id] soft-deletes; POST .../restore undoes inside the recovery window; past it, purge is final. Both cookie-only.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/data-export, GET /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/data-export, GET /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/data-export/download, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/[id], POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/restore · Entities: workspace_exports, activity_log, workspaces · Features: FEAT-EXP-001, FEAT-WS-003

Why it matters: highest blast radius in the system — irreversible data movement; the audit trail is the only evidence anyone pulled the tenant archive.

Architecture behind the API

One layer of depth: Client → Edge → Gateway → Handlers → Postgres RLS / RPCs / deferred workers / external services. If the gateway hangs, every route hangs; if an RPC misbehaves, it bypasses RLS by design and has the widest blast radius.

Component Role Persistence / integrations touched Why it matters for QA
middleware.ts (edge) Session refresh, page-level redirects (matcher excludes static assets and public prefixes) Supabase Auth cookies Matcher mistakes expose pages; stale sessions cause redirect loops
withApiHandler (lib/api/handler.ts) Identity resolution, four-posture auth gate, capability checks, canonical error envelope, request logging, x-request-id — Every handler inherits auth behavior here; a regression here is global
resolveIdentity() + lib/api/middleware/bearer.ts + lib/api/user-jwt.ts Cookie vs PAT unification into one Principal with an RLS-scoped client access_tokens, access_token_secrets PAT regressions break all CLI/CI/agent workflows; parity is structural, not per-route
Route handlers (app/api/v1/**, 79 route.ts + app/api/openapi + app/auth/*) Business operations via RPCs and direct writes through principal.db Per-route posture + requires list are the AuthZ surface to contract-test
SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (bunkai_create_run, bunkai_mark_run_step, bunkai_finish_run, bunkai_sweep_abandoned_runs, applyBillingCheckoutWebhookEvent, …) Escalated, transactional writes Multiple tables at once Bugs inside RPCs bypass RLS entirely — widest blast radius
RLS policies (bunkai_user_role, bunkai_is_workspace_*, migration 0005) Per-row authorization All tenant tables Policy holes = cross-tenant privilege escalation (BK-117/BK-134 class)
after() workers (imports, data-export) Deferred long work outside the request cycle Jira REST, Supabase Storage (workspace-exports path in lib/workspace-export) Function kill mid-work = silent stuck jobs; no external queue
Vercel Cron + CRON_SECRET Daily digest (GET entry point is load-bearing — BK-882) and the pg_cron run sweep notifications, Resend; runs (sweep) Wrong secret = 401 forever; missing GET = silent no-digest

Deployment shape: single Next.js 15 App Router app on Vercel serverless; no separate backend service (aligns with infra-context map). Error envelope is {success:false, error:{code,message}} with x-request-id on every response.

Discovery gaps

What could not be verified on 2026-10-10, and drift found between the legacy map and current code.

Open gaps

  • Overview figures deferred: diagram-design style gate not resolved (no .diagram-design marker).
  • Invite email wiring: legacy recorded "copy-link only, no Resend call in the invite route" — not re-verified this pass; confirm planned vs intentional before writing tests that expect an email.
  • OpenAPI path-level security declarations: schemes are documented, but per-path security was not verified — auth requirements live in handler postures, so spec-only consumers cannot tell a public route from a protected one.
  • api/schemas/ sync is partial — full bun run api:sync not run this session; most surfaces lack generated *.types.ts.
  • Rate limits: a rate_limited error code exists in the envelope family, but per-endpoint limits are undocumented and unimplemented in code (infra map agrees).
  • .env.example has no STRIPE_* or CRON_SECRET entries visible to this pass's sources — where webhook signing secret and cron secret are configured was not re-verified without reading a real .env (not done, by policy).
  • Feature flags: legacy noted a feature_flags table with no runtime reads — not re-verified.
  • Ownership-transfer endpoint: legacy gap (data-map says ownership transfers, never invites; no route found) — still not located.
  • Jira import Beta (FEAT-JIRA-001): staged credentials missing on staging (BK-142) — end-to-end import could not be traced against a live Jira instance.
  • Journey cap decision: six journeys documented (cap 7). Native bugs and the module-tree authoring prelude are folded into the author-run-verdict journey rather than given their own sections; their state machines remain owned by business-data-context.
  • business-data-context and business-e2e-context maps were placeholders at generation time — entity/feature cross-reference ids above come from the legacy feature map and the domain map, not from generated data/e2e maps.

Drift found (legacy map vs current code, 2026-10-10)

  • PAT storage: legacy said personal_access_tokens; current tables are access_tokens + access_token_secrets (migration 0008; hash isolated from the readable token row).
  • Auth surface expanded: legacy journey 1 used only magic-link; current code also ships password signin, signup, confirm, resend, check-email, and OAuth GitHub/Google (/auth/oauth/[provider]).
  • Capability enforcement is now verified per route (legacy: "unverified"). The gateway requires an explicit posture on every route; auth: 'required' lists a non-empty capability tuple enforced before the handler runs. Scope escalation bugs BK-117/BK-134 remain historical records, not current code paths.
  • Cookie-only posture is structural (new): token issue/revoke, active-workspace switch, membership leave, workspace delete/restore, and data-export/download all reject Bearer callers at the gateway.
  • Cron helper moved: isValidCronSecret() now lives in lib/notifications/send-digest-run.ts (legacy cited it in the route file); GET is the load-bearing Vercel Cron entry (BK-882), POST is the manual retry — both gated identically.
  • Webhook hardening: constructEventAsync (Bun-compatible) instead of sync construct; application delegated to RPC applyBillingCheckoutWebhookEvent; async payment events handled; unknown_session deliberately 5xxs so Stripe redelivers.
  • GET /api/v1/imports (collection list) no longer exists — only POST and GET /api/v1/imports/[id].
  • Route count drift: legacy said 81 route.ts under app/api; current tree has 79 under app/api/v1 plus app/api/openapi/route.ts (plus app-level app/auth/callback and app/auth/oauth/[provider]).
  • Infra-map cross-check: the generated infra-context map claims Supabase Storage is unreferenced; current code uploads export archives via supabase.storage in lib/workspace-export/export-runner.ts — the infra map's Storage line is stale for exports and should be corrected on its next UPDATE pass (report only; not edited here).
